title: We accidentally made an AI platform: Jamie Turner

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary focus is Convex as a developer platform that other engineers build generative AI applications on, with platform-level features like reactive backend APIs, vector indexing, and a components framework. Convex is described as a substrate for software builders, with 90%+ of projects being generative AI applications built on the platform. The platform is already in production with widespread gen AI adoption, and new platform initiatives (vector indexing, startups program, components framework) are being announced. Requires familiarity with React, reactive programming, and backend engineering concepts to fully understand the reactive backend paradigm. A recorded live conference talk at the AI Engineer World's Fair in San Francisco. All supporting evidence is directly stated by the speaker in the transcript.

summary: Jamie Turner from Convex delivered a talk at the AI Engineer World's Fair titled "We accidentally made an AI platform." Convex's core mission is to replace traditional backend engineering—the glue work, system configuration, and data format mapping—that consumes roughly half of teams' time without directly benefiting users. Their solution is a high-level API with a functional interface native to applications, similar to Firebase or Parse. Convex drew heavy inspiration from React's functional reactive data flow, where state changes automatically trigger updates in dependent components. However, this paradigm breaks down at the server level, where developers must poll, invalidate caches, and build custom push mechanisms. Convex solves this by pervasively tracking data flow and dependencies through the backend, making queries universally subscribable entities that applications receive updates from as soon as data changes. The AI connection emerged organically: reactive entities in Convex include server-side actions, not just client applications. A simple example is a note-taking app performing ASR, summarization, embedding generation, and related note discovery, with the app brought in at checkpoints. A more sophisticated example is developer webdev Cody's recipe app that generates project plans with concurrent chains for project names, feature requests, color palettes, and icon ideas, all flowing into the application as results arrive. This seamless synchronization proved highly valuable for generative AI, with over 90% of Convex projects being gen AI post-ChatGPT. Convex responded with three initiatives: vector indexing support rolled out late last year, a Convex for Startups program with dedicated forums and events, and an upcoming components framework encapsulating state machines as building blocks for sophisticated AI workflows co-developed with customers.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: React Inspiration and Reactive Backend

sections.title: AI Connection and Application Examples
